content.text:
I rewrote `0.html`. It still looks the same, a black circle centered on the page. I haven't opened it in a browser to check.

- **Small screens:** the circle now shrinks to fit (up to 90% of the screen's shorter side) instead of always being 400px and getting cut off.
- **No stray scrollbars:** the old `width: 100vw` made the page slightly too wide on systems with visible scrollbars, so I removed it. I also used `dvh` so the page fits mobile screens correctly when the browser's toolbar shows or hides.
- **Simpler centering:** the layout uses a two-line grid instead of flexbox, and every element now sizes the same way (`box-sizing: border-box`).
- **Accessibility:** the SVG is marked as an image with a title, so screen readers can announce it.
- **Easy to recolor:** the circle uses `fill="currentColor"`, so you can change its color by setting `color` in CSS.

If you meant a different kind of improvement, like a new look, animation or interactivity, tell me what you have in mind.
